chunks: Hamdan al-Diwani narrated from al-Ridha عليه السلام that he said:

Whoever visits me despite the distance of my abode, I will come to him on the Day of Judgment in three places until I deliver him from its terrors: when the records are scattered to the right and the left, at the Sirat, and at the Mizan.

key_terms.أَهْوَالِهَا: its terrors; the fearful hardships of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ: the Sirat, the bridge or path associated with the final passage
key_terms.الْكُتُبُ: the records or books of deeds given to people
key_terms.الْمِيزَانِ: the Scale by which deeds are weighed
key_terms.زَارَنِي: visited me; refers to performing ziyārah of Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام
key_terms.مَوَاطِنَ: stations or places; specific moments or locations of trial
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, when all people are resurrected and judged

ai.seo_question: What reward is promised for visiting Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام from a distant place?
ai.summary: This hadith states the great merit of visiting Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام even from far away. It promises his assistance on the Day of Judgment at three terrifying stations: the distribution of records, the Sirat, and the Mizan.
